events.title: OSHA grants permanent variance to CBNA/Halmar for Potomac River Tunnel compressed-air work
events.summary: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) issued a final notice granting a permanent variance to CBNA/Halmar Joint Venture for construction of the Potomac River Tunnel Project in Washington, DC. The variance permits the contractor to deviate from three specific OSHA compressed-air standards (29 CFR 1926.803(f)(1), (g)(1)(iii), and (g)(1)(xvii)) by using alternative decompression protocols based on the 1992 French Decompression Tables, staged decompression with oxygen supplementation, and existing man-locks instead of a separate decompression chamber. OSHA determined the alternatives provide worker safety equivalent to or exceeding the standard requirements.

events.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump takes more aspirin than doctors recommend, briefly tried compression socks for ankle swelling but stopped because he disliked them, and regrets undergoing advanced imaging because it generated health scrutiny. The report documented that Trump gets little sleep, has struggled to keep his eyes open during televised events, strains to hear in meetings, lacks regular exercise, and consumes a diet heavy on salty and fatty foods. Trump has covered bruising with makeup and concealed other health ailments. A cardiologist dismissed Trump's aspirin regimen as medically unsound.
events.why_relevant: The report documents presidential health concerns and deliberate concealment of medical information, raising questions about transparency regarding the president's fitness for office and the accuracy of official health statements.
events.basis: Trump gets little sleep and has recently struggled to keep his eyes open during several televised events in the West Wing. Aides, donors and friends say they often have to speak loudly in meetings with the president because he strains to hear.

events.title: Trump posts about Iranian protests and military readiness

We are locked and loaded and ready to go." The post signaled potential U.S. military intervention in response to Iranian government actions against protesters.

events.title: Iran's leadership responded to Trump's military threat
events.summary: Ali Shamkhani, a top adviser to the Ayatollah, warned that any foreign threat to Iran's national security would be met with a response that would make the aggressor regret it. Ali Larijani, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said the American people should be mindful of their soldiers' safety and accused Trump of starting "dangerous adventurism."
events.why_relevant: The escalatory response from Iranian leadership to Trump's military threat increases the risk of military confrontation and demonstrates how unilateral threats can trigger reciprocal hostile declarations.
events.federal_nexus: Trump's prior threat of military action against Iran prompted this response.

events.title: Trump threatens Iran with military intervention over protest crackdown
events.summary: Trump posted on Truth Social that if Iran "violently kills peaceful protesters," the U.S. "will come to their rescue," stating "We are locked and loaded and ready to go." The threat came as economic protests swept Iran and at least 7 people were killed in violence surrounding demonstrations. Iranian officials, including Ali Larijani and Ali Shamkhani, responded with counter-threats, warning against U.S. intervention and alleging the U.S. was stoking the protests.
events.why_relevant: The exchange of explicit military threats between the U.S. and Iran escalates regional tensions and raises the risk of unintended military conflict during a period of domestic Iranian unrest.
events.basis: Trump warned Iran on Truth Social that if it 'violently kills peaceful protesters,' the US 'will come to their rescue.' 'We are locked and loaded and ready to go,' Trump wrote.
